Among patients who ever had an anti-ribonuclear protein result of 16 or higher, I want to follow up the three whose liver enzymes stayed in the normal range. The normal range for GPT is below 60. For each patient, take their highest GPT value among their laboratory tests that fall in the normal range. Rank patients from that highest value down; if two patients share the same value, the one with the smaller patient ID comes first. Please return exactly three patients, one row per patient, with only each patient's Birthday.

g AS (SELECT l.id, MAX(CASE WHEN l.gpt < 60 THEN l.gpt END) AS maxnormal, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE l.gpt >= 60) AS nabove
      FROM laboratory l JOIN r ON r.id = l.id GROUP BY l.id)

FROM g JOIN patient p ON p.id = g.id
WHERE g.nabove = 0 AND g.maxnormal IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY g.maxnormal DESC, g.id ASC

misses.question: I want to know whether molecular saturation is associated with carcinogenicity in our compound library. Please report, for molecules in which every bond is a single bond: the number of carcinogenic molecules minus the number of non-carcinogenic molecules. And for all other molecules: the same difference (carcinogenic count minus non-carcinogenic count). Rules: label '+' means the molecule is carcinogenic; label '-' means non-carcinogenic; bond type '-' denotes a single bond; each molecule belongs to exactly one of the two groups.

misses.predicted:
WITH mol_sat AS (
  SELECT m.molecule_id, m.label,
         NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type IS DISTINCT FROM '-') AS all_single
  FROM molecule m
)
SELECT all_single,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE label = '+') - COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE label = '-') AS carcinogenic_minus_non
FROM mol_sat
GROUP BY all_single;

misses.question: I'd like a ranked inventory of every molecule in the toxicology database that contains at least one carbon atom. For each qualifying molecule, give me its molecule id, carcinogenicity label, number of atoms, number of bonds, number of carbon atoms, number of chlorine atoms, number of carbon-touching bonds, and number of multiple bonds - one row per molecule, including molecules where some of these counts are zero. Rank the rows from the most carbon-touching bonds to the fewest; break ties by larger total atom count, then by molecule id ascending. Give consecutive rank positions 1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps after ties.
misses.evidence: A carbon-touching bond is a bond with a carbon atom at one of its ends; a bond between two carbon atoms counts as one bond. A multiple bond is a double or triple bond. The carcinogenicity label '+' means carcinogenic, '-' means not carcinogenic.
misses.predicted:
WITH carbon_mol AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'c'
),
atom_cnt AS (
  SELECT molecule_id,
         count(*) AS n_atoms,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE element = 'c') AS n_carbon,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE element = 'cl') AS n_chlorine
  FROM atom GROUP BY molecule_id
),
bond_cnt AS (
  SELECT molecule_id,
         count(*) AS n_bonds,
         count(*) FILTER (WHERE bond_type IN ('=', '#')) AS n_multiple
  FROM bond GROUP BY molecule_id
),
cb AS (
  SELECT b.molecule_id, count(*) AS n_carbon_bonds
  FROM bond b
  WHERE b.bond_id IN (
    SELECT c.bond_id FROM connected c
    JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id
    WHERE a.element = 'c'
  )
  GROUP BY b.molecule_id
),
base AS (
  SELECT m.molecule_id, m.label,
         COALESCE(ac.n_atoms, 0) AS n_atoms,
         COALESCE(bc.n_bonds, 0) AS n_bonds,
         COALESCE(ac.n_carbon, 0) AS n_carbon,
         COALESCE(ac.n_chlorine, 0) AS n_chlorine,
         COALESCE(cb.n_carbon_bonds, 0) AS n_carbon_bonds,
         COALESCE(bc.n_multiple, 0) AS n_multiple_bonds
  FROM molecule m
  JOIN carbon_mol cm ON cm.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
  LEFT JOIN atom_cnt ac ON ac.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
  LEFT JOIN bond_cnt bc ON bc.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
  LEFT JOIN cb ON cb.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
)
SELECT molecule_id, label, n_atoms, n_bonds, n_carbon, n_chlorine, n_carbon_bonds, n_multiple_bonds,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY n_carbon_bonds DESC, n_atoms DESC, molecule_id ASC) AS rank
FROM base
ORDER BY rank;
misses.gold: WITH carbonbonds AS (SELECT a.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS carbon_bond_count FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a ON c.atom_id = a.atom_id WHERE a.element = 'c' GROUP BY a.molecule_id), moleculestats AS (SELECT m.molecule_id, m.label, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id) AS atom_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id) AS bond_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'c') AS carbon_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'cl') AS chlorine_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-') AS multiple_bond_count FROM molecule AS m WHERE m.molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'c')), ranked AS (SELECT ms.molecule_id, ms.label, ms.atom_count, ms.bond_count, ms.carbon_count, ms.chlorine_count, COALESCE(cb.carbon_bond_count, 0) AS carbon_touching_bonds, ms.multiple_bond_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(cb.carbon_bond_count, 0) DESC NULLS LAST, ms.atom_count DESC NULLS LAST, ms.molecule_id NULLS FIRST) AS position FROM moleculestats AS ms LEFT JOIN carbonbonds AS cb ON cb.molecule_id = ms.molecule_id) SELECT position, molecule_id, label, atom_count, bond_count, carbon_count, chlorine_count, carbon_touching_bonds, multiple_bond_count FROM ranked ORDER BY position NULLS FIRST
